# Palette fixtures

Inputs and expected outputs for the palette tests (the Rust tests under `core/native/tests/` and the Lua specs under `tests/`). The JSON files are data only; the tests read them as they are.

- `cases.json`: which highlight dump goes with which expected token file, with the colorscheme name, the `background` option and the terminal background each case is derived with (`terminal_canvas`, `null` when the canvas comes from `Normal`). `expected_differences` lists the tokens a case must give differently from its expected file, with the values it must give.
- `user_hl.json`: the highlight groups of a tokyonight storm setup with `transparent = true` and its own group overrides, so `Normal` has no background.
- `user_tokens.json`: the 35 palette tokens that setup must give on a terminal background of `#222436`, plus `table_radius_px`.
- `user_live_hl.json`: the same setup dumped from a headless Neovim, with every group the palette rules read (`_colors_name`, `_background` and `groups`).
- `mocha_hl.json`, `latte_hl.json`: catppuccin.nvim's mocha and latte flavours dumped from a headless Neovim, in the same form.
- `mocha_tokens.json`, `latte_tokens.json`: the 35 tokens each flavour must give (`tokens`) and where each comes from (`sources`). `from_refs` names the tokens whose values the reference renders use, `spec_lifts` the tokens where the contrast floor (4.5:1 for text) deliberately changes a reference value, and `by_rule` the tokens no reference render shows, pinned to what the rules give.
- `vscode_registry_check.json`: for 25 VS Code themes, the theme type, the colors each theme defines and the live `--vscode-*` values VS Code 1.139.1 gives a markdown preview for 26 color ids. The registry port must predict every one of these values.
- `vectors.json`: unit vectors of the palette rules: the visibility floor, the contrast lift, the 7:1 muted text, the mix to a contrast, flattening a translucent color, and whole derivations on small inputs with their expected tokens. It has 14 visibility vectors, 18 contrast vectors, 3 muted, 2 mix, 4 flatten and 21 derivation vectors.
- `registry_defaults.json`: VS Code's color registry defaults for every id the rules know, in all four theme types, as VS Code 1.139.1 resolves them (`null` where VS Code has none). The registry port must give each of these 104 values exactly.
- `bits.json`: the exact 64-bit results of the color math (OKLab, OKLCH, the way back at a shifted lightness, relative luminance, contrast against `#222436`, CIELAB L*) for 300 colors, written as hex bit patterns, so a change in rounding anywhere shows. Computed on one machine; see `bits_libm.json` for the C library's part.
- `bits_libm.json`: the C library's answers behind `bits.json`. `pow`, `atan2`, `cos` and `sin` are the only functions the color math takes from the C library, and their last bit differs between C libraries. It holds every call made for the 300 colors and for the two colors a unit test pins, with argument and result bits, and per color the calls it makes. A unit test answers the calls from this table, so the bit checks hold on any platform, and `palette_bits` also checks this platform's own C library wherever it answers the same.
